title: Checkpoint: Detection Without Tools
prompt:
The course's detection discipline, integrated: invariants + reasoning replacing the sanitizers this image cannot run.

Implement a tiny ownership ledger exactly as specified — the tests probe every failure mode by observable state, the way the module taught you to detect bugs without ASan:

```c
#define LEDGER_CAP 8
typedef struct { int ids[LEDGER_CAP]; int count; } ledger_t;
void ledger_init(ledger_t *lg);              /* count = 0, ids zeroed */
int  ledger_acquire(ledger_t *lg, int id);   /* 1 ok; 0 duplicate; -1 full */
int  ledger_release(ledger_t *lg, int id);   /* 1 ok; 0 missing */
int  ledger_live(const ledger_t *lg);        /* number of live ids */
int  ledger_audit(const ledger_t *lg);       /* 1 if count in [0,CAP] and no duplicate ids; else 0 */
```

tests.name: acquire and release lifecycle
tests.hint: Acquire adds, release removes exactly once; a second release of the same id reports missing.

tests.name: duplicate acquire rejected
tests.hint: A double-acquire is the ledger's use-after-free: it must be rejected, not double-recorded.

tests.name: capacity respected
tests.hint: The ninth acquire reports full without corrupting the eight live entries.

tests.name: audit catches corruption
tests.hint: A healthy ledger audits clean; forcing a second entry to share id 3 is corruption the audit must catch.
